Subject: Post-call recap & next steps - Data residency / region pinning

Hi Alice / Bob -

Thanks for the time earlier today - good discussion. Quick recap and proposed next steps while we loop in engineering:

Summary from today's discovery call:
- Primary concern: ensure all customer PII and model request/response data remains in-country (US) for regulated product flows.
- Secondary concern: logging/trace data and backups - retention and geo-location requirements.
- Business ask: confirm whether Redwood can guarantee region pinning for production traffic and what cross-region failover behavior looks like.

Action items / next steps:
1) Rishi (me) to provide a written summary of Redwood's region-pinning options and how backups/logging are handled (below).
2) We will attach SOC 2 summary and an architecture diagram for the region-pinning flow.
3) Schedule a technical follow-up with Aditya to walk the security/infra team through options. Proposed times: Thu 2/26 10-11am PT or Fri 2/27 1-2pm PT.

Preliminary answers (high level):
- Region pinning: Redwood supports account- and route-level region pinning. You can pin production traffic to a single cloud region (e.g., us-west-2) to ensure inference and associated ephemeral artifacts remain in that region.
- Cross-region failover: By default we support configurable failover policies (automatic failover to a secondary region if primary capacity/health is compromised). For strict residency requirements we can disable automatic cross-region failover and require manual failover.
- Backups & snapshots: Persistent backups (model checkpoints, customer-config snapshots) are stored encrypted and can be scoped to the same region; we can also write backups to a customer-managed bucket in the same region when required.
- Logs & retention: Audit logs and request logs are configurable; retention windows and log export destinations (customer-managed SIEM/S3) can be defined per-account.

I'll follow up with the SOC 2 summary and the region-pinning architecture diagram attached. Please confirm whether the requirement is strictly "US-only (no backups outside US)" or whether a US primary with a nearby failover region would be acceptable.

Thanks -

Thanks Rishi - good summary. A few clarifications from our side:

1) Residency scope: For regulated customers in our banking product we require all PII and request/response data to remain in the US. That includes backups and any replicated storage. Logs with identifying info must also be kept in the US by default.
2) Failover behavior: We want the ability to disable automatic cross-region failover. In an outage scenario we will decide whether to failover to a secondary region after our internal approvals.
3) Encryption & key control: We prefer that backups and persistent storage be encrypted with a customer-managed key (KMS) where possible. Can Redwood support CMK for backups?

Also cc'ing Bob from our security team to confirm any additional compliance asks.

--Alice

Alice / Bob -

Thanks - great notes. Below are concrete answers to your items and a couple of recommended configurations based on similar bank deployments. Aditya I've put you on CC to confirm the infra specifics.

Answers / Recommendations:
- "US-only" scope: Yes - we can configure an account so that all inference requests, ephemeral caches, and persistent snapshots are kept in a single AWS region (e.g., us-east-1 or us-west-2). For strict residency we recommend pinning both the serving route and the backup export target to the same region.
- Cross-region failover: We offer three modes: (1) automatic failover to a pre-configured secondary region, (2) manual failover (operator-initiated), or (3) no failover (fail closed). For Acme's requirements we can set the default to manual failover and add a playbook for how Redwood can assist in a coordinated failover.
- Backups & encryption: We support customer-managed keys (CMK) for backups and persistent exports. We can also configure exports directly to a customer-managed S3 bucket in the specified region.
- Logs / retention: Audit and request logs can be exported to a customer-managed destination (S3, Splunk, or SIEM) in-region. Retention windows are configurable; we typically set 90 days by default but can extend or shorten per contract.
- Replication / KV cache: Runtime KV caches are ephemeral and remain in-region with the serving node; we do not replicate KV caches cross-region unless configured for explicit active-active setups. Persistent state (snapshots) is what we replicate for DR.

Attachments: SOC 2 summary + architecture diagram are attached for your security team review. I've also uploaded a short mutual action plan to HubSpot (link below).

- Alice/Bob: confirm whether manual-only failover and US-only backups meet your compliance check so we can move to contract language.

Subject: Re: Post-call: Data residency & region pinning - technical clarifications

Quick internal / technical notes to confirm before the 2/26 call:

- Region pinning mechanism: We apply a routing policy at the control plane that binds a customer's serving routes to a set of compute pools in a given cloud region. Serving nodes, KV cache, and ephemeral storage are provisioned in that region.
- Failover triggers: Automatic failover is triggered by health checks and sustained capacity degradation; manual failover is also supported via our ops console or API and can be run by Acme with our documented playbook.
- Backups: Snapshot backups are taken periodically and stored encrypted at rest. For strict residency we can write snapshots to a customer-managed S3 bucket in the same region (requires a short onboarding to grant write-only permissions).
- CMK support: We support customer-managed KMS keys for persistent exports/backups; it requires adding the CMK ARN to the account config during provisioning.
- Logs: Audit and request logs can be exported in near real-time to a customer-managed destination. We can also redact PII on export if required (configurable).

Note: for maximum compliance (no risk of cross-region copies), recommend the Private deployment option - gives you full control over network egress and S3 endpoints. We should surface that as an option in the upcoming commercial proposal.
